intuition: First collect each tree level from left to right using a queue. Reverse the collected values on every other level. Keep the queue traversal itself in the same order, which makes the alternating output easier to manage.

Keep the queue in ordinary left-to-right BFS order. At the start of each round, its current size is the number of nodes on this level. Consume only that many entries while appending their children for the next level. This prevents children from being mixed into their parents’ result.

Reverse the collected values on alternate levels. Leaving queue order unchanged is important: reversing traversal direction and still appending children left-first can scramble the following level. Separating traversal from display makes the invariant simple and handles sparse trees without special directional child rules.

steps: For root=[3,9,20,null,null,15,7], initialize queue=[3], result=[], and left_to_right=true.
The first level has one node. Pop 3, collect [3], and enqueue its children 9 then 20.
Append [3] unchanged and switch direction. The next queue is [9,20].
Process exactly two nodes: 9 contributes no children; 20 appends 15 and 7. Collected values are [9,20].
Because this level is right-to-left, reverse that output to [20,9]. The queue still contains [15,7].
Process the final level in the normal direction and append [15,7]. Return [[3],[20,9],[15,7]].

approach: Collect the current level left to right.
Reverse its values when this level’s direction is backward.
Toggle direction and continue with the next level.
concept.correctness: Ordinary breadth-first grouping gives each level’s true left-to-right values. Applying the required display direction to each group changes only that group’s ordering. Since queue traversal remains consistent, subsequent level groups are still correct, and alternating the display flag produces the zigzag result.

complexity.explanation: Every node is visited once and every level is reversed at most once. Queue memory follows tree width; all displayed values occupy output memory.
